x: Lamarck was the first to put a theory of evolution before the public, in 1809 (inheritance of acquired characters). Mendel founded genetics and de Candolle coined taxonomy.
t: Recall the pioneer behind each first.

x: The smallpox vaccine, made by Edward Jenner in 1796 from cowpox, was the world's first vaccine. Polio vaccine came much later from Salk.
Option C is incorrect: Christiaan Barnard performed the first heart transplant in 1967 in Cape Town, South Africa, not Australia. Barney Clark got the first artificial heart in 1982.
t: Check the place in each statement.

x: A is true: Watson and Crick proposed the double-helix model of DNA in 1953. R is false because DNA polymerase I was discovered by Arthur Kornberg in 1956.
t: Check who is credited with each discovery before judging R.
s:
Assertion (A): Watson and Crick first proposed the double-helix model of DNA in 1953.
Reason (R): Watson and Crick also discovered the enzyme DNA polymerase I.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Dolly being a sheep says what she was, not why she was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.
t: Check whether R is a reason or only a description.

x: Both are true: insulin was the first human hormone made by recombinant DNA, and Humulin was the first rDNA drug, approved in 1982.
All four are correct firsts: triticale is the first man-made cereal, hCG the first placental hormone, OAA the first product of C₄ fixation and IgM the first antibody in an infection.
Lamarck first explained evolution to the public, de Candolle coined "taxonomy", Golgi first saw the Golgi body and Miescher first isolated DNA (nuclein), giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the pioneer behind each first.

x: All four are correct: Dolly was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, Samrupa the first cloned buffalo, Ganga India's first cloned cow and Injaz the first cloned camel.

Lamarckism was the first broad theory of evolution, Archaeopteryx fossils came from Solnhofen, Louis Lartet found the first Cro-Magnon skull and the Denisovan was identified in 2010, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
A.P. de Candolle first used vascular tissues to classify plants, and he also coined "taxonomy".
All four are correct: Schleiden and Schwann gave cell theory, prokaryotes were the first life, McClintock found jumping genes and Mendel crossed peas first.
DNA polymerase I was the first DNA polymerase found, by Arthur Kornberg, and yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) was the first eukaryote fully sequenced, in 1996, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
Both are true: hCG is human chorionic gonadotropin, and the embryo's heart starts beating around the fourth to fifth week.
Oxaloacetic acid is abbreviated OAA, the first stable product of carbon fixation in C₄ plants.
t: Recall OAA as the C₄ first product.

x: Both are true: India's first biodiesel plant was at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, and Jonas Salk made the first successful polio vaccine.
t: Recall the firsts in India and medicine.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: Saheli (centchroman) was the first non-steroidal oral contraceptive, and Hyderabad has India's first dinosaurium.
India's first dental college was R. Ahmed Dental College in Kolkata, founded in 1920, and Jaya was India's first dwarf rice variety, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
Both are true: Bhutan became the first country to ban the sale of tobacco, in 2004.
Both are true: Karl Landsteiner first classified blood groups (ABO) in 1900.
t: Recall the discovery of blood groups.

x: William Harvey described blood circulation in 1628. Landsteiner found blood groups and Jenner made the first vaccine.
Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are the earliest organisms known from fossils, about 3.5 billion years old. Archaeopteryx and Cro-Magnon are far later.

Option C is incorrect: radiocarbon dating works only up to about 50,000 years on once-living material; the oldest rocks are dated by the uranium–lead method. The Archaeopteryx, litmus and Cro-Magnon statements are right.
t: Recall the age range each dating method can measure.
o: Archaeopteryx is the earliest known bird.
Litmus is the oldest form of pH indicator.
Radiocarbon (C-14) dating is used for dating the oldest rocks and ancient mountains.
Louis Lartet discovered the earliest Cro-Magnon skull in 1868.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the oxygen-free early atmosphere explains the conditions life arose in, not why the first life was unicellular.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a background condition.

x: Uranium–lead dates the oldest rocks, Louis Lartet found the first Cro-Magnon skull, litmus is the oldest pH indicator and the early atmosphere had no free oxygen, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the facts about early Earth and dating.

x: All four are correct: farmers were the first biotechnologists, seed grades go nucleus → breeder → foundation → certified, Archaeopteryx links birds and reptiles and Cro-Magnons date to 30,000–45,000 years ago.
Arthropoda, with insects, crustaceans and spiders, is the largest animal phylum, holding over three-quarters of known species.
Option C is incorrect: the cell is the smallest unit of life, while viroids are the smallest infectious agents. Mycoplasma and prions are described correctly.
t: Discriminate the smallest living unit from the smallest pathogen.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: being the largest internal organ is a separate record, not the reason it is the largest gland.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a parallel record.

x: The stapes is the smallest bone, the femur the largest, the stapedius the smallest muscle and the sartorius the longest muscle, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
I, II and III are correct: the cerebrum is the largest part of the brain, the neuron the longest cell and the monocyte the largest WBC. IV is false because the liver is the largest gland.

The colossal squid is the largest invertebrate, the king cobra the longest venomous snake, the aye-aye the largest nocturnal primate and Kitti's hog-nosed bat the smallest bat, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
All three are correct: Kitti's hog-nosed bat is the bumblebee bat, and flying foxes, such as the giant golden-crowned flying fox, are the largest bats.
Both are true but R does not explain A: being the largest living animal does not by itself make it the largest ever; that also needs comparison with extinct animals.
t: Check whether R is a cause or a narrower record.

x: The blue whale is the largest mammal, the African elephant the largest land mammal, the gibbon the smallest man-like ape and the sperm whale has the largest brain by absolute size, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Separate largest overall, largest on land and largest brain.

(c) Smallest man-like ape
(d) Largest brain by absolute size

List-II
(i) Gibbon

x: All three are correct: the elephant has the largest brain on land, the ant the largest brain for its body size and the kangaroo rat survives longest without drinking.
Rafflesia arnoldii produces the largest single flower, up to about a metre across. The other options are animals.
The femur is the longest bone, the ileum the largest part of the gut, the aorta the largest artery and WBCs the largest blood cells, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
Option C is incorrect: the longest cell is the neuron; the sartorius is the longest muscle. The Guinea worm, ileum and duodenum facts are right.
t: Discriminate the longest cell from the longest muscle.

x: A is true: the kangaroo rat can live without drinking water. R is false because the Guinea worm is the longest nematode infecting humans.
t: Check the organism named in each statement.

x: The femur is the longest bone, the sartorius the longest muscle, the stapedius the shortest muscle and the neuron the longest cell, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
All three are correct: the duodenum is the shortest part of the small intestine, the ileum the longest, and the femur the longest bone.
t: Recall the parts of the small intestine.
